headline: Govt had no better alternative to fuel price hike, says PM's adviser
summary: Prime Minister's adviser Zahed Ur Rahman stated the government had no alternative but to raise fuel prices, acknowledging it would undeniably increase public suffering, but hoped for public understanding.
details: Prime Minister's adviser Zahed Ur Rahman stated the government had no alternative but to raise fuel prices, acknowledging it would undeniably increase public suffering. He made these remarks during a weekly briefing at the Secretariat.

Rahman noted that no government would deliberately make such an unpopular decision ahead of local government elections. He expressed hope that citizens would understand the necessity behind their elected government's decision at this moment.

The adviser clarified that the recent fuel price hike was not imposed as a condition by the International Monetary Fund (IMF). He also dismissed concerns about a political crisis despite recent incidents like crude bomb explosions and bus fires in Dhaka.

Following the fuel price hike, bus fares have increased by 17 paisa per kilometer, and launch fares have seen a 17-20% rise. Truck fares have reportedly increased arbitrarily, while motorcycle ride-sharing in Dhaka has seen a 20-50 Taka hike.
caption:
Bangladesh government states it had no alternative but to raise fuel prices, despite knowing it would increase public suffering.

The adviser clarified that the recent fuel price hike was not imposed as a condition by the International Monetary Fund (IMF). He also dismissed concerns about a political crisis despite recent incidents like crude bomb explosions and bus fires in Dhaka.

Following the fuel price hike, bus fares have increased by 17 paisa per kilometer, and launch fares have seen a 17-20% rise. Truck fares have reportedly increased arbitrarily, while motorcycle ride-sharing in Dhaka has seen a 20-50 Taka hike.

headline: 279 Bangladeshi men to be recruited for government jobs in Brunei via BOESL
summary: Bangladesh Overseas Employment and Services Limited (BOESL) is facilitating the recruitment of 279 male workers for various government-approved positions in Brunei. The roles include construction workers, technicians, and drivers, with attractive salaries and
details: Bangladesh Overseas Employment and Services Limited (BOESL) is recruiting 279 male workers for government-approved jobs in Brunei. The application deadline is September 26, 2026, by 4 PM. This presents a significant opportunity for Bangladeshi job seekers.

The available positions span various sectors, including construction workers (180+), plumbers, masons, foremen, welders, electricians, carpenters, and drivers. There are also roles for AC technicians, farm workers, operators, and general laborers.

Salaries vary, with some positions offering a monthly wage of 600 Brunei Dollars (approximately BDT 57,866). Other roles provide a daily wage of 20-22 Brunei Dollars (approximately BDT 1,929-2,122), depending on the specific job.

Applicants must apply through the BOESEL website and pay a non-refundable application fee of BDT 200. Final selected candidates who pass health examinations will be required to pay a service charge to BOESEL.

The service charge is BDT 56,350 for skilled workers and BDT 44,850 for semi-skilled/unskilled workers, which includes VAT registration and other ancillary costs. This fee must be paid via a pay-order to "BOESEL, Dhaka" at Sonali Bank, Mogbazar branch.

Successful candidates will receive additional benefits, including company-covered accommodation and food expenses. The employer will also bear the airfare, and medical, insurance, and leave facilities will be provided according to Brunei's labor laws.
The employment contract is for two years, renewable upon mutual agreement. The standard working hours are eight hours per day. Further details are available on the BOESEL website.
